seoDescription: Learn how to build your first website with Python and Flask in this beginner-friendly tutorial. This video guides you through setting up a project with a virtual environment, installing Flask, and creating your first application. You'll discover how to define routes, render HTML templates for different pages, and integrate the Bootstrap CSS framework to add a responsive navigation bar. By the end, you will have built a simple, multi-page static website, understanding Flask's core concepts for rapid web development.

chapters.title: Introduction to Flask Web Development
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the Flask web framework and outlines the plan to build a very simple static website quickly.

chapters.title: Prerequisites and Tool Setup
chapters.description: This chapter covers the necessary tools for the project, including Python, the Git Bash terminal, and the Sublime Text editor, and where to download them.

chapters.title: Creating the Project and Virtual Environment
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to create a project directory and set up a Python virtual environment to isolate project dependencies.

chapters.title: Installing Flask and Its Dependencies
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to create the main application file and install the Flask framework using pip within the activated virtual environment.

chapters.title: Creating the First "Hello, World!" App
chapters.description: This chapter walks through writing the minimal Python code required to create a Flask app instance, define a root URL route, and return a simple string.

chapters.title: Serving HTML with Templates
chapters.description: This chapter explains how to stop returning simple strings and start rendering full HTML files using Flask's render_template function and the templates directory.

chapters.title: Integrating the Bootstrap Framework
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to quickly improve the website's appearance by integrating the Bootstrap CSS framework and adding a navigation bar component.

chapters.title: Customizing the Bootstrap Navbar
chapters.description: This chapter involves cleaning up the default Bootstrap navbar code by removing unwanted elements like the search form and dropdown, and customizing the brand link.

chapters.title: Building a Multi-Page Website
chapters.description: This chapter details how to add a second page to the website by defining a new route in Flask, creating a new HTML template, and updating the navbar for navigation.

chapters.title: Recap and What's Next
chapters.description: This chapter summarizes the simplicity of Flask, discusses how the project already implements parts of the Model-View-Controller pattern, and previews future topics.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.description: The video concludes by summarizing what was covered and providing calls to action for liking the video, subscribing, and checking out Codemy.com.

summary: ## Introduction to Flask Flask is a lightweight and minimalist Python web framework, often called a "micro-framework." It's designed to be simple, flexible, and fast, allowing you to build web applications quickly without a lot of boilerplate code. This video demonstrates building a basic static website in just a few minutes. ## Initial Setup & Environment Before writing code, set up the project environment: 1. **Create a Project Directory**: `mkdir my_flask` 2. **Create a Virtual Environment**: Use a virtual environment to manage project-specific dependencies. ```bash python -m venv virtual ``` 3. **Activate the Environment**: * Windows: `source virtual/scripts/activate` * Mac/Linux: `source virtual/bin/activate` 4. **Install Flask**: Use pip to install Flask and its dependencies inside the activated environment. ```bash pip install Flask ``` > [!TIP] > Always use a virtual environment for your Python projects to avoid dependency conflicts. ## Creating a Basic Flask App The core of a Flask application is a single Python file (e.g., `app.py`). **Key Code Structure**: * **Import Flask**: `from flask import Flask, render_template` * **Create App Instance**: `app = Flask(__name__)` * **Define a Route**: Use the `@app.route()` decorator to map a URL to a Python function. * **Create a View Function**: This function handles requests for the associated route and returns a response. ```python # app.py from flask import Flask, render_template # Create a Flask Instance app = Flask(__name__) # Create a route decorator @app.route('/') def index(): return render_template("index.html") ``` ## Running the Development Server Use the `flask` command to start the local development server, which runs on `http://127.0.0.1:5000` by default. ```bash flask run ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > By default, the Flask development server does not automatically reload when you make code changes. You must stop the server (`Ctrl+C`) and restart it (`flask run`) to see your updates. This will be addressed in a future video. ## Using HTML Templates Instead of returning plain strings from view functions, use **templates** to serve full HTML pages. * **`render_template()` Function**: This Flask function finds and renders an HTML file. * **`templates` Directory**: By convention, Flask looks for HTML files in a folder named `templates` in your project's root directory. ## Building a Multi-Page Site To add more pages, simply repeat the pattern of creating a route, a view function, and a corresponding HTML template. 1. **Add a new route in `app.py`**: ```python @app.route('/about') def about(): return render_template("about.html") ``` 2. **Create `about.html` in the `templates` folder**. 3. **Add links in your HTML** to navigate between pages (e.g., `About`). ## Key Takeaways * **Simplicity**: Flask allows you to create a functioning website with just a few lines of code. * **Separation of Concerns**: The application logic (Python in `app.py`) is kept separate from the presentation layer (HTML in the `templates` folder). * **MVC Pattern**: This structure represents the **View** (HTML templates) and **Controller** (Python view functions) of a Model-View-Controller architecture. The **Model** (database) will be covered in future lessons.
